items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: When Earl Hines had his little band and was playing for afternoon things in Pittsburgh, the boys after the session would come and get me. They'd come and get me and take me to play

ctx.x: to do that. When Earl Hines gave his little dances in Pittsburgh - I think he was about 6 or 7 years older than any of us - they had a tough gang from downtown come out and try to break up the dances, fight, and they did a little bit of everything - Soho gang. When Roland stepped out, the street car wasn't going fast enough for them to jump on the street car and try to get away because he'd break up the gangs and everything. He was a terrific man.
Do you want to get into the Buck and Bubbles?
